A.reason: Shows that n=4 with a single group, no control and no test cannot support 'significantly improved' or causal claims; notes rival explanations.
Correctly computes post mean 8.00 and gain 4.50. Cites specific A03 conflicts: Q2/Q4 totals and S1 pretest items summing to 2 against a reported 3.
A01 observation notes record an animal-diet lesson, so magnetism-specific needs are not traceable to the cited evidence. Supported by the material and not on the card.
Test validity unclear: the confidence item is counted in the score, scoring was teacher-administered, and no reliability or validation is reported. This fits R02's accepted alternative.
No themes, excerpts or quotes support the qualitative claims; the findings are asserted only.

B.reason: Single-group n=4 design with no control or significance test cannot support causal or significant-effect claims.
Instrument is unvalidated and has no reliability evidence; it includes a confidence item and is teacher-scored. Matches R02's alternative.
Two thresholds (0.78 vs 0.80) are verifiable in the text, and expert relevance ratings do not establish effectiveness. Substantive and supported.
Qualitative claims lack quotes, excerpts and coding evidence.
Global, scalable and replicable claims are disproportionate to one school, four students and one topic; the authors' own limitations contradict them.

C.reason: Causal and 'significant' claims rest on an n=4 single-group pre/post design with no control; rival explanations are listed.
Test validity problems: confidence item, teacher-administered, no reliability or content validation. Fits R02's alternative.
Near-identical rating vectors, inconsistent cut-offs and a relevance scale applied to quality items are verifiable from Table 4 and the text.
No quotes, codes or trustworthiness procedures; Figure 2 shows labels only.
Overgeneralisation to a scalable global model from four students; the subgroup claims are uninterpretable. Supported by the text.
